subject: cleanup
text: cap cleanup has now stripped a genuine non-obvious-constraint comment/docstring twice in one session on the windows project: once the DUPLICADO enum comment in models.py (docs-centralize task), once the _construir_configuracion docstring explaining why the settings Toplevel is withdrawn-not-destroyed (roster-signal task) — both caught only by live git-diff inspection before commit, both corrected via cap send. The cleanup consult seems biased toward treating any comment near a short/clearly-named function as redundant, without checking whether it documents a cross-cutting invariant (like a threading/lifecycle constraint) that the function's name and body don't express. Consider tightening the cleanup prompt in the agents skill or cap-cleanup to explicitly ask 'does this comment explain something a background thread, a different caller, or a later maintainer could not infer from the code alone' before removing it.
